newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes rise, ANS May trade over.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes rise, ANS May trade over.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices climbed Thursday in line with a modest rise in energy futures, while local trade ended for May deliveries, traders said.
June crude oil, the current futures contract, rose 30 cents a barrel to $20.03 on reports U.N oil monitors were arrested in Northern Iraq by a Kurdish faction.
The reports revived dull trade on the NYMEX crude oil futures exchange, with market players speculating the arrests could jeopardize oil-for-food supplies from Iraq.
Ship traffic on the Panama Canal continued normally despite a sunken tug, according to an employee of the Canal Zone Authority.
May trade on the West Coast appeared over and players spent the morning requesting shipping space on ARCO's Line 63 pipeline, traders said.
ARCO expects to announce its shipping allotments on the line early Friday.
Sales of Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude were flat Thursday, with the last deal done two weeks ago at $1.32 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude.
Buyers speculated that BP Oil's below-average spot sales for May were forcing them to ship crude to U.S. Gulf market or store more in Alaska.
BP declined to comment on the rumors.
Inventory levels remained "normal" at Alaska's Valdez terminal, where ANS is stored before being shipped south, said an official for Alyeska Pipeline Service Co, the terminal's operator.
He said the terminal's 9.18 million-barrel-capacity was only 62 percent full.
Separately, Alyeska officials said tankers leaving Valdez stayed on schedule Thursday despite large ice chunks that occasionally stopped traffic.
Outright prices for May ANS stood 20 cents higher than yesterday at line with increases in spot May WTI.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.
Traders reported no deals in Line 63 and heavy California grades.
